newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish, foreign telecom firms move to agreement.
newsitem.headline: Polish, foreign telecom firms move to agreement.

text.p: Polish state-owned telecom firm TPSA and its foreign partners in the Centertel SA joint venture, a mobile phone operator, has moved to an agreement after a long row over power-sharing, Centertel said on Friday.
Spokesman Jacek Kalinowski said Centertel's foreign partners, France Telecom and Ameritech Corp, had agreed to meet TPSA's demands for a bigger say in the company.

"The shareholders have reached an agreement regarding demands of the majority shareholder (TPSA) to control more votes in the management," Kalinowski told Reuters. "Candidates (to the management) are expected to be presented and discussed."
He also said Centertel's new general director, whose post have been vacant for more than a year due to the conflict, was likely to be appointed within several days. @

TPSA and Centertel also clinched a vital deal on fees for interconnection to TPSA's ground network on Thursday, the companies said in a joint statement. Kalinowski said the agreement would be signed after the chief executive was appointed.
TPSA annuled the agreement earlier this year, saying it was dissatisfied with fees paid by Centertel for the use of its ground facilities. @
The cancellation was the last in a series of blows to Centertel, set up in 1991 by TPSA, controlling a 51 percent stake, together with Ameritech Corp and France Telecom, which hold 24.5 percent each.

The partnership turned sour last year when TPSA, arguing its role in the company did not reflect its majority shareholding, began seeking more say in Centertel's management and a bigger share in the company's profits.
Earlier this year TPSA blocked Ameritech and France Telecom's plans to seek for Centertel one of two government licences to use a modern digital GSM system. @
The licences went to two consortia of Polish and foreign companies, which are now launching operations to challenge the position of Centertel, operating an older analogue system.

Ameritech and France Telecom have started intenational arbitration proceedings against Poland's government, saying that back in 1991 they were promised a GSM licence. The government said the promise was not legally binding.
The two companies were not available for comment on how the apparent reconciliation between TPSA and Centertel would affect the proceedings. @

A source close to the telecommunications ministry, who asked not to be named, earlier said Centertel would stand a good chance in a planned tender for a licence to operate a high-frequency DCS cellular system.
Centertel has attracted more than 100,000 customers while analysts say some 1.5 million cellular telephones could be sold in Poland by the year 2000.
